title: api-gateway: tuning streaming proxy buffers and routing rules to stabilize tool-calls and OpenAI compatibility
author: Sofia Mendes
description: Motivation: multiple production incidents and bench tests showed intermittent streaming stalls and malformed function-call payloads when passing large structured outputs through the API gateway streaming proxy, especially under the OpenAI compatibility layer and when requests were routed cross-region or to fallback model variants. This PR adjusts streaming proxy buffer sizing, tightens routing rules for tool/function calls, and adds an OpenAI-compatible chunking/flush policy to ensure stable structured output streaming. Changeset: 1) Increase default proxy stream buffer from 64KB to 256KB with dynamic up-to-512KB growth under bursty writes and high-latency upstreams; 2) Introduce per-route payload_size_limit and structured_output_threshold config keys and default sensible limits to avoid proxy-level fragmentation; 3) Add routing policy to prefer same-region/dedicated pools for requests with tool calls or large structured outputs, with automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained; 4) Implement OpenAI-compatible chunk framing for streaming JSON/function-calls so client parsers receive complete JSON tokens and function call events without mid-chunk truncation; 5) Add defensive parsing and backpressure metrics so we can alert on proxy stalls and partial-chunk reassembly; 6) Add end-to-end tests that exercise streaming tool-calls, structured JSON outputs, and client-side reassembly; 7) Docs and changelog updates describing new route config, limits and upgrade notes. Rollout plan: feature gated behind api-gateway flag, staged rollout to 10% traffic, monitor streaming_reassembly_failures and proxy_write_retries for 48h, then full rollout. Related: ENG-1589 (incident postmortem) and ENG-1623 (latency regression investigation). Checklist: - [x] Add proxy buffer growth logic and config knobs - [x] Add per-route limits and routing preference - [x] Implement OpenAI-compatible chunk framing - [x] Add unit + integration + e2e tests - [x] Update docs and migration notes - [x] Add metrics/alerts and dashboards Impact: This is primarily an API surface stability and performance tweak. It slightly increases default memory usage on gateway nodes when handling many simultaneous large streams but reduces observed request stalls and malformed function-call payloads. Operators should monitor the new metrics and may tune per-route payload_size_limit for extreme workloads.

review_comments: Ethan: Can you justify the default 256KB buffer? How did you pick growth to 512KB? Please include memory impact numbers.

Sofia: Synthetic and prod sampling showed tail stalls at 48-96KB thresholds; 256KB gives headroom without large memory tax. Growth to 512KB only occurs under sustained bursts per-connection and is capped cluster-wide. Added numbers in docs and a new metric proxy_buffer_bytes_reserved.
Priya: We need better test coverage for the OpenAI chunk framing when the client disconnects mid-chunk.

Sofia: Added teardown and partial-client disconnect tests in integration-tests/e2e/streaming_tool_calls.test.ts which assert reassembly and metrics increment; also added unit tests for the chunker to simulate disconnects.
Marcus: Routing preference is conservative but could impact capacity planning for Dedicated customers. Add a rollout note and a flag to disable per-route preference.
Sofia: Added feature flag api_gateway_toolcall_routing_preference and documented the rollout plan; also added telemetry to measure quota impacts.
Ethan: CI flake observed on e2e initially, reran and passed.
Priya: Approving pending telemetry and docs polish.
Marcus: Approving - looks good to merge.

Operators: monitor api-gateway.proxy_buffer_bytes_reserved, api-gateway.streaming_reassembly_failures, and api-gateway.proxy_write_retries. See docs/migration/2026-02-api-gateway-buffer-upgrade.md for tuning guidance.
